checks.item: predict: preprocess, eval mode, no_grad, alignment
checks.evidence: Uses sprout.preprocess.preprocess, model.eval(), torch.no_grad(). A probe model started in train mode with Dropout(0.9) was called with (training=False, grad_enabled=False); batched output (batch_size=3, 8 rows) matched single-batch preprocess+softmax; o.path == manifest order; labels come from class_map[row label] in the same row order; empty manifest gives (0,N) probs; corrupt image raises UnidentifiedImageError rather than being silently skipped; CMYK image handled.

Plan signature is predict(model, manifest_split); implementation adds a required class_map dict and batch_size. Justified by the global constraint that class order comes from the saved class map: it keeps the labels from being derived by sorting or from a hardcoded list, and the labels stay aligned with probability columns. Later tasks can use it by passing the checkpoint's class map. The cost is that every caller must pass the map; flagged in notes.
No legacy/ changes in the task diff, no secrets found in src/sprout/eval, no earlier tests modified (new files only: eval/*.py, tests/test_metrics.py, pyproject.toml and docs/PLAN.md edits)

notes: (1) predict leaves the model in eval mode and does not restore the previous mode; callers that keep training afterwards must call model.train() themselves. (2) macro_f1 on empty input raises (max of empty array), and selective_metrics returns nan rates when nothing is answered; later tasks must handle that. (3) No repo test covers macro_f1 with a prediction-only class, and the implementation differs from sklearn's default there; it follows docs/TESTING.md, so later reports should say so. (4) preprocess does not apply EXIF rotation; that is pre-existing and outside T2.2, but predict inherits it. (5) mcnemar_exact is a hand-rolled binomial; verified against scipy. I did not break code and re-run tests, since the independent recomputation covered the statistics instead.
